original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R be a finitely generated noetherian K-algebra domain, let L = Q(R), and let delta be a K-derivation of R. If X_delta^f denotes the abelian group of all delta-integral factors occurring for delta-integral elements of L, must X_delta^f be a finitely generated abelian group?

refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R be a finitely generated noetherian K-algebra domain with quotient field L=Q(R), and let δ:R→R be a K-derivation. Call a nonzero element h∈L δ-integral if there exists b∈R such that δ(h)=bh; such a b is called a δ-integral factor of h. Let X_δ^f={b∈R : there exists a nonzero h∈L with δ(h)=bh}, viewed as a subgroup of the additive group (R,+). Must X_δ^f be a finitely generated abelian group? ([cmjpapers.math.cas.cz](https://cmjpapers.math.cas.cz/full/63/2/cmj63_2_17.pdf))
